messages:
ana-peopleops: Quick q for the group - new hire Lina has an EAD pending and wants a vaccine medical exemption for benefits. What docs do we accept?

matt-peopleops: We need a provider letter for benefits. For I-9/immigration we still require ID/auth docs (EAD card or receipt + passport). @raj-immigration any red flags?

raj-immigration: Clinician letter should state the medical reason, date, clinician name and contact. License number preferred. If documents are from outside the US, include certified English translations. We can help prepare an explanatory note for consular questions.

lina-newhire: My doctor can provide a note but it might omit a license number on first pass. Also I have an I-797C receipt and passport. Is that enough to start benefits?

ana-peopleops: Receipt + passport + medical letter (scan) is fine to start benefits enrollment. Ask the clinic to add clinic contact info if license not on note. Upload to the HR portal by Friday so benefits can process.

matt-peopleops: For onboarding/I-9: scanned PDFs are acceptable initially. We will do an originals check within 3 business days of start if the EAD is still pending. We'll document the exception.

raj-immigration: If you plan to travel for stamping, bring originals and translations. We can draft a short one-page summary for you to carry.

lina-newhire: Thanks everyone - Ill upload tonight and flag when done. Would appreciate the summary letter.

imm-bot: Reminder set: "Check Lina uploads" in 48h.

ana-peopleops: Great, once uploads are in benefits@redwood.com will confirm retro dates. Lina, ping if you need the summary letter ASAP.
